# PULL REQUEST // CHANGE

> **A change is easier to understand when we can see what relationship changed, why it changed, and what was carried forward.**

## What changed?

Describe the change in the shortest useful way.

## Why?

What problem, limitation, opportunity, or idea led to this change?

## What relationship changed?

Describe the relationship affected by this work.

That might be between a person and a tool, one component and another, a project and its history, software and its environment, one machine and another, information and the person using it, or something else.

## What was preserved?

What continuity, provenance, behavior, identity, or spirit needed to survive the change?

If something intentionally did **not** survive, explain why.

## What was gained?

What is now easier, clearer, safer, more powerful, more expressive, more continuous, or more useful?

## What was lost or traded?

Did the change increase complexity, remove compatibility, alter behavior, introduce maintenance cost, or close off another possibility?

Not every change has a meaningful loss. If there is not one, say so.

## How was it verified?

Describe what you tested or inspected.

Include relevant tests, commands, screenshots, logs, comparisons, commits, or other evidence.

## Does this affect licensing, provenance, or third-party material?

If you introduced code, artwork, documentation, dependencies, or other material from somewhere else, identify where it came from and what license applies.

If not, say **no**.

## Anything else?

Add whatever context a reviewer needs to understand the change.

---

**A pull request is not only a diff. It is a record of transformation.**
